output_json.diff_review: Diff touches exactly two files: core/src/main/java/.../ArchiveAnalyzer.java and core/src/test/java/.../ArchiveAnalyzerTest.java. It does not touch the POV files under .security-pipeline/pov (confirmed by inspecting patch_only.diff, which contains no .security-pipeline paths). The main-code change adds a small private static helper `isFileWithinDestination(File destination, File file)` that compares canonical paths (fail-closed on IOException), and inserts a check right after `final File file = new File(destination, entry.getName())` in extractArchive() — before the directory-entry mkdirs branch and before the engine.accept()/extractAcceptedFile branch — so this single insertion point covers all three sink traces called out in the alert (line 518 mkdirs, line 543 parent.mkdirs, line 547 FileOutputStream), for both ZIP-family and TAR archives since they share extractArchive. It also applies the same guard to the independent GZIP and BZIP2 single-file paths in extractFiles(), which build `new File(destination, uncompressedName)` separately and were flagged in the regression_hint as an additional bypass vector. The fix is also robust against absolute-path entries: even if `new File(destination, "/etc/passwd")`-style construction were to yield an absolute path outside destination, its canonical form would not start with destination's canonical path + separator, so it is correctly rejected. On containment failure, the entry is skipped (continue / warn) rather than aborting the whole extraction — consistent with the analyzer's existing error-tolerant style, and this is a reasonable, minimal remediation choice, not a functionality removal (legitimate entries still extract, confirmed by the new test's safe.txt assertion). The test-file change adds one well-scoped JUnit regression test (testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip) exercising the real private extractFiles method via reflection with both a malicious traversal entry and a benign entry, asserting the malicious one is blocked and the benign one still extracts — this is an appropriate regression test, not a POV modification or a weakening of test coverage. No unrelated or overly broad changes were introduced.

Result: BUILD SUCCESS, 'Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 1' — same skip count as observed in the orchestrator's regression logs; the skipped test (testFileFilterIsValid, guarded by assumeFalse(isPreviouslyLoaded(...))) is a pre-existing class-loading-order guard unrelated to this patch. The new testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip test passes, confirming both the traversal block and continued normal extraction of legitimate entries.
output_json.summary: The patch adds a canonical-path containment check (isFileWithinDestination) immediately after each `new File(destination, ...)` construction from untrusted archive entry names in ArchiveAnalyzer.java, covering the shared choke point in extractArchive (both the directory mkdirs sink and the extractAcceptedFile parent.mkdirs()/FileOutputStream sinks named in all three alert traces) as well as the GZIP/BZIP2 single-file decompression paths. Entries resolving outside the destination are skipped with a warning instead of being written. Independently reran the POV and regression tests via the docker wrapper: POV now exits 1 ('NOT VULNERABLE') on the patched worktree (was exit 0 pre-patch), and ArchiveAnalyzerTest (including the new testExtractFilesBlocksZipSlip regression test) passes with BUILD SUCCESS, with only a pre-existing, unrelated class-loading-guarded test skipped (present before and after the patch).
